markdown_report:
**Recommendation:** retain the fixed 0.5 terminal/reconstruction BERT4Rec objective and add a bounded audit of sampled versus full-catalog competition. At 40% progress, this provides useful evidence before committing budget to optimizer interventions.

**Insights from the starting point.** First, sampler and serialized-serving checks pass across all four categories. This supports interpreting predictions within tested coverage, without establishing recommendation quality. Second, recent-item deletion lowers mean target scores in every category. Its diagnostic hit@10 intervals include zero, so greater recency emphasis remains an unverified training hypothesis. Third, equal branch coefficients do not imply equal optimization influence. Target counts and loss denominators must remain explicit when evaluating the proposed mixture.

**Insights from related work.** First, BERT4Rec distinguishes masked reconstruction from future-item prediction [1]. Terminal assessment therefore provides a relevant complement to reconstruction margins. Second, sampled ranking metrics can reverse model comparisons [2]. Strong separation from random negatives cannot establish full-catalog top-10 performance. Third, negative-sampling choices can affect popularity groups differently [3]. Training-frequency strata can expose heterogeneity, although those published findings do not predict gains here.

These insights organize into three directions: supervision allocation, candidate competition, and measurement reliability. Their common framework is:

| Direction | Existing evidence | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|
| Allocation | Fixed mixture with sequence means | Sustained terminal benefit |
| Competition | Random-negative margins | Eligible-catalog boundary |
| Reliability | Serving parity passes | Diagnostic predictive value |

Three atomic proposals follow; scores denote originality/potential/difficulty, with higher difficulty meaning harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Positive and negative assessment |
|---|---|---|
| **Paired catalog-boundary audit** [2,3] | 4/7/3 | Originality: integrates paired strata; established ingredients. Potential: identifies hidden competition; remains in-sample. Difficulty: chunked scoring is simple; eligibility needs care. |
| Corruption-preserving one-target reconstruction control [1] | 3/6/4 | Originality: isolates supervision variance; standard estimator. Potential: clarifies reduction effects; does not match terminal context. Difficulty: reuses masks; requires sampler instrumentation. |
| Transactional branch-omission audit [4] | 5/6/8 | Originality: optimizer-aware adaptation; established influence methods. Potential: measures local transfer; weak evidence for lasting gains. Difficulty: reuses losses; exact rollback is demanding. |

**Selected algorithm.** Freeze one trained model per category. Preselect up to 32 training users/category and one eligible endpoint/user independently of scores. Score each identical appended-MASK query against both 99 fixed unique negatives and every eligible real item, using chunked inference. Report target ranks, paired hit@10 disagreement, target-minus-tenth-competitor margins, and tenth–eleventh competitor gaps, stratified by training frequency and visible-history length. Define frequencies from training interactions only; preserve complete-prefix exclusions and deterministic ties.

Set a compute cap before execution and report incomplete coverage explicitly. These measurements diagnose candidate competition; they neither establish generalization nor change model selection. Preserve the host macro validation HR@10, all four routes, seeds, interfaces, and one checkpoint/category. References [1–4] are linked below.

idea.description: Add a preregistered, bounded paired sampled/full-catalog boundary audit to the fixed 0.5 terminal/reconstruction BERT4Rec experiment, using exactly one frozen trained model per category.
idea.motivation: Supplied diagnostics establish serving consistency and conditional history sensitivity, but provide neither host validation gains nor full-catalog ranking evidence. Comparing identical training-prefix queries across candidate sets tests whether strong random-negative margins conceal competition near the top-10 boundary. This is particularly relevant because the native simulator requests full-catalog unseen-item recommendations, while selection remains the pinned sampled macro validation HR@10.
idea.implementation_notes:
Keep the corrected BERT4Rec architecture and preregistered objective unchanged: average supervised losses within each sequence, average sequences within each branch, then combine branch means with coefficients 0.5 and 0.5. Record branch counts, target counts and denominators; do not infer gradient shares from coefficients. This proposal adds measurement, not adaptive reweighting or a second predictor.

Before execution, declare at most 32 users/category, endpoint eligibility, frequency/history bins, candidate seed, tie policy and a diagnostic compute cap within the remaining shared budget. Remaining runtime is unspecified, so do not promise additional training controls. Select users without inspecting scores. Choose one public training endpoint per user with at least four preceding interactions and a target absent from the complete preceding prefix. Never use later events to determine candidate eligibility. Report excluded users and reasons.

Build the serving query from at most maxlen-1 preceding items, left pad, append the reserved MASK, and read its actual final nonpadding position. Never use count-1 or include the target as visible input. Keep absolute positions identical across candidate-set comparisons. Use eval mode and the same scoring dtype for both candidate sets. Validate candidate scoring through view.log2feats and view.predict_score; retain view.item_emb and view.model as the actual trained network.

Eligible competitors are all real catalog IDs excluding complete-prefix items and the target. PAD and MASK never compete. Sample 99 unique competitors with a dedicated generator; insufficient pools yield an explicit unavailable result. Score the eligible catalog in chunks using the same query feature, without fitting a retrieval model. Use descending score and ascending item ID for deterministic diagnostic ordering. The host evaluator remains untouched.

Compute sampled and full-catalog target ranks, hit@10, and their paired disagreement counts. Define target margin as target score minus the tenth-highest eligible competitor score. Define the boundary gap as the tenth-highest minus eleventh-highest competitor score. Insufficient competitor counts produce unavailable values. With identical scores and nested competitors, full-catalog target rank cannot improve over sampled rank; use this as a consistency check. Nonfinite scores invalidate the affected example.

Stratify descriptively by target frequency counted exclusively from training histories and visible-history length, using bins frozen before outcomes are inspected. Catalog frequency is descriptive and does not create a separately fitted popularity score. Unobserved items are unlabeled competitors, not known dislikes. Record counts and raw paired outcomes; avoid strong conclusions for small strata. User-bootstrap intervals, if budgeted, describe sampled-user uncertainty conditional on the fitted model and candidate construction, not training-seed uncertainty or generalization.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Return metrics and metric_definitions with actual dataset identity, completion counts, definitions, exclusions, nonfinite observations and elapsed time. Keep the B x L loader contract and family-specific sample_batch. Gate serving-sensitive interpretation on sampler and serialized-serving parity. Preserve existing measured probes and explicit availability reporting. Restore each module's training flag and all touched RNG states in finally blocks; use dedicated diagnostic generators and avoid advancing the training iterator.

A timed-out audit reports completed coverage and the stopping reason, without claiming complete four-category results. Aggregate category means with equal category weights only when all four categories are available; never substitute a partial macro. Do not change the objective, sampler or checkpoint choice in response to these audit users within the same preregistered experiment.

Preserve Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl routing; preprocessing seed 0; training seed 42; maximum 200 epochs; 200 batches per epoch; single-GPU execution; DATA_DIR=os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; and trial-local artifacts. Export exactly one checkpoint/category through the matching predictor writer. Retain full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for five designated real training users/category. Use only permitted public histories, titles, descriptions and timestamps. Select solely through unchanged host macro validation HR@10; do not access hidden tests, other trials or checkpoints. No validation or full-catalog improvement is claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
preregister user cap, bins, seed, eligibility, ties and compute cap
for category in the four required routes:
    train one corrected BERT4Rec using the fixed 0.5 objective
    export its single checkpoint and matching predictor
    require sampler and serialized-serving parity before interpretation
    preserve model modes and touched random states
    try:
        model.eval()
        select training users and endpoints without inspecting scores
        for user, endpoint in selected examples:
            stop with explicit partial status if compute cap is reached
            prefix, target = public_training_prefix(user, endpoint)
            eligible = real_items - set(prefix) - {target}
            if len(eligible) < 99:
                record unavailable example; continue
            query = left_pad(prefix[-(maxlen-1):] + [MASK])
            feature = log2feats(query)[actual_final_nonpadding_position]
            target_score = predict_score(feature, target)
            sampled = sample_99_unique(eligible, dedicated_generator)
            score eligible items in chunks with the same feature
            rank using descending score then ascending item ID
            compute sampled/full ranks and hits
            compute target-minus-tenth-competitor margins
            compute tenth-minus-eleventh competitor gaps
            assert full_rank >= sampled_rank
            record paired outcomes and frozen descriptive strata
        return metrics, metric_definitions, counts, status and elapsed time
    finally:
        restore module modes and touched random states
aggregate equal-weight category summaries only if all four are available
# Audit results do not adapt training or replace host validation.
select using the unchanged host macro validation HR@10

originality.positive: Combines identical-query candidate comparisons, explicit top-10 boundaries and training-frequency strata within the constrained BERT4Rec workflow.
originality.negative: Candidate-set audits and popularity stratification are established techniques; the contribution is their controlled integration.

future_potential.positive: Can reveal whether apparent sampled-pair strength survives catalog competition and motivate a focused subsequent single-model experiment.
future_potential.negative: Training-prefix findings remain in-sample and may not predict host validation gains or future-item full-catalog performance.

code_difficulty.positive: Reuses frozen encoder features and chunked item scoring, with no optimizer rollback or architecture changes.
code_difficulty.negative: Complete-prefix eligibility, deterministic ties, category aggregation and reliable partial-result reporting require careful implementation.

related_work.title: [1] BERT4Rec: Sequential Recommendation with Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformer
contributions: Uses bidirectional masked-item reconstruction for sequential recommendation.
Uses an appended mask for next-item inference, motivating explicit terminal assessment.
limitations: Does not establish the best terminal/reconstruction allocation for the supplied corrected host baseline.
Provides no evidence of gains for this proposed audit.

related_work.title: [2] On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can produce inconsistent model comparisons.
Motivates distinguishing sampled-candidate performance from full-catalog competition.
limitations: Does not justify changing the pinned host evaluator.
Does not determine the magnitude of candidate-set effects in these four datasets.

related_work.title: [3] Performance and Bias of Negative Sampling
contributions: Reports dataset-dependent accuracy and popularity-group tradeoffs under different negative-sampling choices.
Motivates reporting training-frequency strata alongside aggregate results.
limitations: Its findings do not establish that popularity-based sampling improves this corrected BERT4Rec.
Descriptive frequency strata cannot establish exposure mechanisms or user preferences.

related_work.title: [4] LESS: Selecting Influential Data for Targeted Instruction Tuning
contributions: Uses optimizer-aware gradient information for targeted influence estimation.
Provides methodological inspiration for the alternative branch-transfer audit.
limitations: Studies a different learning setting and supplies no BERT4Rec validation evidence.
Local influence estimates do not establish sustained ranking improvement.
